data.incumbent: PayPal (implied by the PayPal/Venmo button concerns and the account manager complaints; the transcript never names the incumbent explicitly)

evidence.excerpt: They were launching Canada, then the UK, and sitters have to get paid locally.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Expansion into Canada and UK created local sitter payout need.

evidence.excerpt: called it "a haunted house."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel, VP of Engineering
evidence.note: Customer's own description of their payments code.

evidence.excerpt: Two engineers more or less full-time just keeping sitter payments working.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Engineering burden of maintaining existing payments; 'more or less' is hedged.

evidence.excerpt: a roadmap item, faster pay for sitters, that had been pushed three quarters in a row.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Faster sitter pay roadmap item repeatedly delayed.

evidence.excerpt: Daniel. He signed.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Daniel signed the deal.

evidence.excerpt: The CFO joined one call for ten minutes, asked one question, "does this change when sitters get paid?", and left.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: CFO
evidence.note: CFO's only concern was sitter pay timing; limited involvement.

evidence.excerpt: "this is an engineering decision, finance will sign what I bring them."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Daniel stated early that engineering decides and finance signs off.

evidence.excerpt: Their account manager had changed three times in two years.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Incumbent service churn, reported by customer to rep.

evidence.excerpt: "I've stopped learning their names."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Customer frustration with incumbent account manager turnover.

evidence.excerpt: A lot of pet owners pay with PayPal and Venmo, and they were nervous about what happens to those buttons.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Customer worry about preserving PayPal/Venmo checkout.

evidence.excerpt: They had a call with Braintree in the middle of the evaluation.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Braintree was consulted; inferred from question changes, not directly witnessed.

evidence.excerpt: I know because the questions changed. It went from "how fast can we build this" to "what do we lose."
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Observed shift in customer questions from speed to loss.

evidence.excerpt: Do we lose PayPal, do we lose Venmo, what happens to the saved cards.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Specific loss concerns raised after Braintree call.

evidence.excerpt: I assume Braintree told them they'd lose things. I don't know that. That's me guessing.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Rep explicitly flags guess about what Braintree said.

evidence.excerpt: One of their engineers, on her own time, built a working sitter payment flow over a weekend and showed it at Monday standup.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Engineer-built prototype validated docs/sandbox.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the docs and the sandbox.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Docs and sandbox drew positive reaction.

evidence.excerpt: And the marketplace piece. Onboarding sitters, the identity checks, paying out in local currency.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Marketplace features got reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Silence: the acceptance-rate slide.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Acceptance-rate slide drew no reaction.

evidence.excerpt: "our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Why auth-rate pitch fell flat: low booking value.

evidence.excerpt: The weekend prototype. Before that it was a bake-off.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Prototype is when rep felt it was won; prior was a competitive bake-off.

evidence.excerpt: After that Daniel stopped saying "if."
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Observed change in Daniel's language from if to when.

evidence.excerpt: Nothing, really. It was a clean one.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Rep says nothing couldn't be shown; contradicted later.

evidence.excerpt: We kind of danced around it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Admits evasive handling of PayPal/Venmo question.

evidence.excerpt: We said they could keep offering PayPal and we'd work through the details in implementation.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: PayPal answer deferred to implementation.

evidence.excerpt: I didn't have a crisp answer on Venmo in the room, and I still don't.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Venmo question unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: They decided it was a risk they'd take.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Rep's characterization of customer's risk acceptance; source unclear.

evidence.excerpt: We walked them through moving saved cards over so nobody has to re-enter anything. But it was a doc and a conversation.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Saved card migration only covered by doc and conversation, no proof.

evidence.excerpt: "who's done this at our size without losing cards?"
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Customer asked for a reference at their size.

evidence.excerpt: I said I'd get back to him. I didn't.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Follow-up on reference request never happened.

evidence.excerpt: Once, in the kickoff. His engineer said, "we'll find out."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel's engineer
evidence.note: Saved-card question resurfaced at kickoff, still unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: "Payments shouldn't be a team," he said that a lot.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Recurring customer phrase about payments burden.

evidence.excerpt: "We want to stop babysitting this."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Daniel
evidence.note: Customer's words for the desired outcome.

evidence.excerpt: On the sitter side it's "paid by Friday." The whole promise to sitters is paid by Friday.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Sitter promise is paid by Friday.

evidence.excerpt: Nobody there says "marketplace." They say "the app."
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Customer says 'the app', not 'marketplace'; conflicts with our pitch term.

evidence.excerpt: And nobody says "payouts." They say "sitter pay."
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Customer says 'sitter pay', not 'payouts'.

evidence.excerpt: Only that I barely sold this. Their engineer did.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Priya
evidence.note: Rep's view that customer's engineer drove the win.

contradictions.what: Rep said customer asked for nothing they couldn't show and it was 'a clean one', then admitted dancing around PayPal/Venmo and having no crisp Venmo answer.
'Clean one' conflicts with the unfulfilled saved-cards reference request, raised again at kickoff.
Daniel is named as decider, but rep says their engineer sold it and she 'barely sold this', suggesting influence beyond Daniel.
Rep says she 'knows' Braintree call happened because questions changed, yet admits she doesn't know what Braintree said; the call is inferred.
Rep says the customer 'decided it was a risk they'd take' on PayPal/Venmo, but earlier says the details were deferred to implementation and Venmo was unanswered.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Answered 'Nothing, really. It was a clean one.' then later admitted dancing around PayPal/Venmo and an unanswered saved-cards reference request.

language_pairs.theirs: haunted house; payments shouldn't be a team; stop babysitting this

outcome_signals.what: Felt won after the weekend prototype; Daniel stopped saying 'if'.
PayPal/Venmo unresolved at signing; customer accepted the risk, so part of the business may not have moved cleanly.
Saved-card reference request went unanswered after signing; still open at kickoff.
